overview: Capgemini SE is a Paris-headquartered global IT services, consulting and engineering group with FY2025 revenues of €22.5bn and roughly 420,000 employees in more than 50 countries (India alone is ~50% of headcount, the core of its 'Rightshore' offshore delivery model). The Group organizes its offer into three businesses – Strategy & Transformation (consulting, 8% of revenue), Applications & Technology (its core, 63% of revenue) and Operations & Engineering (managed services/BPO plus R&D/engineering, 29% of revenue and growing fast after the October 2025 acquisition of WNS Holdings) – sold across five geographic regions: North America (29% of 2025 revenue), Rest of Europe (30%), France (19%), UK & Ireland (13%) and Asia-Pacific & Latin America (9%). Capgemini is now repositioning around 'Intelligent Operations' – agentic-AI-powered business process transformation – as its next growth vector, following its 2020 acquisition of engineering group Altran (now Capgemini Engineering) and 2025's WNS deal.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned by selling technology consulting, application development/modernization, engineering/R&D services and (since WNS) business-process outsourcing, billed under a mix of time-and-materials, fixed-price/deliverable-based and resource-based (staff augmentation) contracts, delivered through a global onshore/offshore blend (66% of the post-WNS headcount of ~418,000 is offshore, principally India). Growth is a combination of organic volume/pricing and bolt-on M&A (WNS and Cloud4C added an estimated ~5 points of FY2026 constant-currency growth). Management's headline profitability KPI is 'operating margin' (APM Capgemini defines it as revenue less operating costs, calculated BEFORE 'Other operating income and expenses' – i.e., before restructuring, M&A amortization/integration costs, share-based comp and pension curtailments), guided at 13.6%-13.8% of revenue for FY2026, versus 13.3% actually delivered in FY2025 and FY2024. Statutory operating profit is materially lower and volatile: it was €878m (7.3% margin) in H1 2026 vs €976m (8.8%) in H1 2025, because 'Other operating income and expenses' rose from €401m to €628m on Fit-for-Growth restructuring – i.e., the operating-margin KPI structurally understates true cash cost of running the business by excluding recurring restructuring, which has run €124m (FY2024) and €205m (FY2025) and is guided to ~€700m cumulative across FY2026-FY2027.

revenue_streams.name: Operations & Engineering (incl. WNS Intelligent Business Operations)
revenue_streams.trend: growing fast (+24.7% cc H1 2026, largely WNS/Cloud4C inorganic)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and public sector; largest sector exposures are Manufacturing (25% of FY2025 revenue), Financial Services (22%), Public Sector (15%), Telecoms/Media/Tech (12%), Consumer Goods & Retail (13%), Energy & Utilities (8%) and Services (5%)
business_model.geographic_mix: North America 29% of FY2025 revenue, Rest of Europe 30%, France 19%, UK & Ireland 13%, Asia-Pacific & Latin America 9%
business_model.contracting_notes: Mix of time-and-materials, fixed-price/deliverable-based, and outsourcing/managed-services (increasingly non-FTE, outcome-based pricing for Intelligent Operations per management commentary). Book-to-bill was 1.08x for FY2025 and 1.04x for H1 2026 (1.07x in Q2 2026 alone), i.e., bookings still running ahead of revenue recognition.
business_model.organic_free_cash_flow_definition: Capgemini's 'organic free cash flow' (the metric management guides on, ~€1.8-1.9bn for FY2026) is NOT the same as statutory OCF minus capex: it equals cash flow from operations, LESS capex (net of disposals), LESS lease-liability repayments (IFRS 16 principal), and ADJUSTED to add back net interest cash outflow. In H1 2026 this bridge was: OCF €357m − capex €114m − net interest cash cost €62m − lease repayments €144m = organic FCF €37m. A naive OCF-minus-capex figure (€357m − €114m = €243m) would overstate the guided metric by ~6.5x because it ignores the ~€144m/half of lease principal Capgemini treats as an operating cost. The DCF model should replicate the company's own bridge (subtract lease repayments and add back net interest) rather than use OCF less capex directly.
business_model.dividend_buyback_policy: Capgemini paid a €3.40/share dividend for FY2025 (flat YoY, €570m cash cost in H1 2026) plus €315m of share buybacks in H1 2026 alone under a stated multiyear return-of-capital program; normalized EPS payout ratio is roughly 26-36% depending on the period, leaving room for continued bolt-on M&A alongside cash returns even as net debt has risen sharply post-WNS.

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global IT services/consulting groups by revenue (~€22.5bn FY2025), the largest France-headquartered player and the #1 or #2 player in several European national markets (UK, France, Benelux, Nordics), but smaller in global scale than Accenture (~$65bn revenue) and structurally lower-margin than Indian heritage players (Infosys guides 20-22% operating margin FY2026 vs Capgemini's 13.6-13.8% target) because of Capgemini's more Europe-weighted, higher-cost onshore delivery mix and lower offshore proportion (66% offshore vs >80% typical at TCS/Infosys/Wipro).

moat_factors.description: ~276,000 offshore staff (66% of headcount), heavily India-based, gives a cost base competitive with Indian-heritage peers, but Capgemini's blended margin still trails pure-play offshore vendors because of its larger onshore/European consulting layer.

moat_factors.factor: Incumbency / switching costs in large multi-year outsourcing and application-management contracts
moat_factors.description: Long-duration managed-services and application-support contracts create recontracting inertia, evidenced by a resilient book-to-bill consistently above 1.0x even through the 2024-2025 European IT-spending slowdown.

Management calls out 'over 50% of services contracts will include sovereignty requirements by 2029, up from 5% in 2025' and cites accelerating European defense/sovereignty demand and the Cloud4C acquisition as a differentiator versus US-headquartered rivals in an era of European data-sovereignty and defense-spending tailwinds.

End-to-end capability spanning Capgemini Invent (strategy), Applications & Technology, and now Intelligent Operations (post-WNS BPO), combined with named partnerships (Microsoft, Google, AWS, SAP, Mistral AI, OpenAI) is positioned as a moat versus narrower pure-play consultancies or BPOs, though the same breadth is claimed by Accenture at greater scale.

moat_factors.factor: Brand/scale in engineering & R&D services (Capgemini Engineering, ex-Altran)
moat_factors.description: Post-2020 Altran acquisition gives unusually deep automotive/aerospace/industrial R&D outsourcing capability versus peers, but this is also a concentrated cyclical exposure (see risks).

weaknesses: Structurally lower operating margin than both Indian offshore-heavy peers (Infosys ~20-22%) and, on a blended basis, Accenture (~14.7-14.9%), reflecting a costlier European/onshore delivery mix

Heavy France/Rest-of-Europe revenue concentration (49% of FY2025 revenue) in the weakest demand region of the cycle: France was -4.1% organic in FY2025 and Rest of Europe -0.7%, only just returning to growth in H1 2026

Newly BPO-heavy business mix (Operations & Engineering, now including WNS, is 29% of revenue) is a lower value-add, more commoditized, more price-competitive segment than consulting or bespoke application development

No dominant single-vendor scale advantage versus Accenture in enterprise AI/cloud transformation deals, and no proprietary hyperscaler platform of its own – Capgemini is a systems integrator/reseller of partner AI stacks (Microsoft, Google, OpenAI, Mistral) rather than an AI platform owner

growth_drivers: Agentic AI-driven 'Intelligent Operations' cross-sell of WNS's BPO/transactional platforms combined with Capgemini's transformation capability – management cites a 'joint pipeline of 100+ opportunities' with WNS and 'several large deals secured in recent months' as of H1 2026

European defense, security and technology-sovereignty spending, flagged by management as an accelerating, largely non-discretionary secular tailwind (Cloud4C acquisition, SAP-Capgemini Sovereign Technology Partnership)
Legacy technology/digital-core modernization spend that management says is a prerequisite for enterprise AI deployment ("a resilient and modern digital core is essential to deploying AI at scale")

Continued bolt-on M&A (WNS $3.3bn, Cloud4C, SEIMAF in FY2025 alone; a long history of one-to-four acquisitions per year) supplementing organic growth by an estimated ~5 points of FY2026 constant-currency growth

Fit-for-Growth restructuring (announced February 2026, ~€700m cumulative cost through 2026-2027) intended to reshape the workforce pyramid and free up margin/investment capacity for AI delivery capability
Recovery in North America (+19.8% cc in H1 2026) and UK & Ireland (+21.1% cc) providing higher-margin growth to offset weaker Continental Europe

business.risk: AI-driven pricing and revenue deflation of the classic staffing-pyramid model
business.description: Capgemini's own FY2025 URD risk factors state plainly that 'Rapid advances in Generative and Agentic AI are re-shaping delivery models, raising external productivity benchmarks more quickly than organizations can adapt. This may create pricing to execution mismatches, resulting in lower margins at sale or material delivery risks,' and separately that AI-driven automation 'increasingly affects lower value and entry level tasks, requiring a reshaping of workforce pyramids.' This is the central bear thesis for the whole sector (Accenture's guidance cut in mid-2025 dragged Capgemini down >8% in a single session on read-through fears) and is not hypothetical – it is already showing up in Applications & Technology's sub-5% growth versus Operations & Engineering's 20%+ (inorganic-driven) growth.

business.risk: Manufacturing/automotive R&D exposure inherited via Altran (Capgemini Engineering)
business.description: Manufacturing is 25% of FY2025 group revenue and was the single weakest sector, -2.1% organic for FY2025 (though it inflected to +4.2% by Q4 2025 and +3.5%/+4.2% in Q1/H1 2026); European automotive OEMs and suppliers have been cutting R&D and engineering-services budgets, directly affecting the ex-Altran engineering business.

business.risk: France/Continental Europe demand concentration in the weakest sub-market
business.description: France (19% of revenue) posted -4.1% organic growth in FY2025 and only just returned to growth (+0.4%/+1.8% in H1/Q2 2026); Rest of Europe (30% of revenue) was -0.7% in FY2025. Nearly half of group revenue sits in the geography that lagged the North America/UK recovery by several quarters.

business.risk: Client/public-sector contract concentration and delivery risk
business.description: Large fixed-price and outsourcing contracts carry cost-overrun and penalty risk per the URD's 'Major delivery service failure' risk factor; Public Sector is 15% of revenue and subject to government budget cycles (France Public Sector was a specific H1 2026 drag even as the rest of France recovered).

financial.risk: Net debt roughly tripled in 18 months on the WNS/Cloud4C acquisition spree
financial.description: Net debt went from €2,107m at Dec-31-2024 to €5,306m at Dec-31-2025 to €6,454m at June-30-2026 (partly seasonal working-capital build, partly a bond redemption/reissuance of €800m in April/May 2026). Gross borrowings reached €9,052m at H1 2026 against cash/cash-management assets of only €2,610m. S&P affirmed Capgemini at BBB+ (stable outlook) but flagged temporarily elevated leverage as a rating consideration pending deleveraging.

financial.risk: Goodwill now exceeds total shareholders' equity
financial.description: Group goodwill jumped from €11,454m at June-30-2025 to €14,674m at June-30-2026 (a ~€3.2bn increase, almost entirely the WNS/Cloud4C purchase-price allocations), against equity attributable to owners of only €11,615m at the same date. A large portion of this goodwill stack also pre-dates WNS and stems from the 2020 Altran deal and the 2000 Ernst & Young Consulting acquisition. Any shortfall versus WNS/Altran cash-generation expectations (e.g., if BPO margins or automotive engineering demand disappoint) creates impairment risk against a balance sheet that is simultaneously more levered.

Currency fluctuations were a -2.5pt headwind to reported H1 2026 growth (-4.0pt in Q1 alone) versus constant-currency growth; with WNS adding meaningful USD/INR-denominated revenue and cost, EUR/USD and EUR/INR translation volatility is now a larger swing factor on reported results than pre-WNS.
ETR jumped from 26.2% (H1 2025) to 37.5% (H1 2026), which management says 'is not necessarily representative of the full year ETR' – a source of EPS noise around acquisition integration.

regulatory.risk: Data protection, AI governance and cross-border data-transfer regulation
regulatory.description: URD risk factors flag 'Data protection failure' and evolving cybersecurity/AI regulation across the EU, UK and other jurisdictions as compliance-cost and liability risks, particularly given the scale of client data Capgemini and the newly-acquired WNS processes in BPO engagements.
The Group flags export-control compliance costs tied to advanced technology/AI platforms and defense-sector work as a growing constraint on its ability to freely mobilize global delivery talent.

macro.description: Constant-currency growth was negative or flat for six consecutive quarters (Q1 2024 through Q3 2025, -3.3% to +2.9%) before inflecting sharply to +10.6% (Q4 2025) and +11.0%/+11.6% (Q1/Q2 2026) – though the 2026 acceleration is substantially inorganic (WNS/Cloud4C added ~6.5pts in Q4 2025/Q1 2026 alone per the Group's own scope-impact disclosure). The underlying organic cycle has only recently turned positive.

URD flags 'inflation-driven cost increases' (salary, energy, real estate, cloud/token costs) that may not be fully passed through to clients, compressing margin; utilization rates in Applications & Technology were 78-80% and in Strategy & Transformation only 67-71% through 2025-2026, leaving limited slack to absorb a downturn without headcount action.

macro.risk: Interest-rate sensitivity via higher post-WNS debt load
macro.description: With gross borrowings now above €9bn (up from ~€5.8bn a year earlier) and net interest cash cost roughly doubling year-on-year in H1 2026 (€38m to €62m), Capgemini's earnings are more exposed to prevailing EUR/USD rate levels than at any point in over a decade.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global IT services/consulting demand troughed through 2024 into mid-2025 on discretionary-budget cuts, with managed/outsourcing services holding up better than transformation consulting; the industry (Capgemini included) is now navigating a bifurcated narrative – AI as a demand driver for large enterprise-wide transformation programs versus AI as a structural deflator of the classic billable-hour staffing pyramid. Capgemini's FY2025 URD explicitly frames Gen/Agentic AI as 'an opportunity or a threat' in the same sentence.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical and discretionary at the consulting/transformation end (Strategy & Transformation, parts of Applications & Technology); more resilient/recurring at the managed-services and outsourcing end (Operations & Engineering, now BPO-heavy post-WNS). The FY2024-2025 downturn showed six quarters of negative-to-flat organic growth before recovering.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate historically (net cash position through 2023), now moderate and rising given the post-WNS debt load (>€9bn gross borrowings, net debt €6.5bn at H1 2026) and BBB+ rating with a 'stable' but leverage-sensitive outlook.
key_input_costs: Personnel/wage costs (68% of revenue, the dominant cost line)
Purchases & sub-contracting (13.7% of revenue in FY2025, rising)
Cloud/hyperscaler and AI 'token' compute costs (newly disclosed as a cost pressure in the FY2025 URD)

recent_developments.event: Capgemini announces definitive agreement to acquire WNS Holdings (BPO/digital business process services) for $76.50/share cash, ~$3.3bn total consideration excluding WNS net debt
WNS acquisition closes; WNS and Cloud4C consolidated into Group results from Q4 2025, creating the new 'Intelligent Business Operations' line within Operations & Engineering

FY2025 results: revenue €22,465m (+3.4% cc), operating margin stable at 13.3%, organic FCF €1,949m (stable), net debt jumps to €5,306m (from €2,107m at Dec-2024) on WNS/Cloud4C; FY2026 guidance issued (+6.5% to +8.5% cc revenue growth, 13.6-13.8% margin, ~€1.8-1.9bn organic FCF); 'Fit-for-Growth' restructuring program launched (~€700m cumulative cost 2026-2027)
Q1 2026 revenues €5,943m, +11.0% cc (of which ~6.5pts inorganic from WNS/Cloud4C); bookings €6,054m, book-to-bill 1.02x; North America +20.7% cc, France still -1.0% cc
Capgemini redeems in full its €800m April-2020 bond at maturity and issues a new €800m bond in May 2026, partially refinancing the post-WNS debt load

H1 2026 results ('Capgemini upgrades its 2026 outlook'): revenue €12,082m (+8.8% reported, +11.3% cc); operating margin 12.5% (+10bps YoY); operating profit down -10.1% to €878m (7.3% margin) on higher Fit-for-Growth restructuring charges (€628m other operating expense vs €401m H1 2025); net profit down -31.3% to €498m; normalized EPS down -11.9% to €5.29; organic FCF only €37m (vs €60m H1 2025, in line with normal seasonality); net debt €6,454m; France returns to organic growth (+0.4%) after five negative quarters; FY2026 constant-currency revenue growth guidance RAISED to +8.5%/+9.0% (from +6.5%/+8.5%); margin and organic FCF guidance maintained

Stock has materially de-rated over the trailing 12 months (roughly -30%+ peak to mid-2026) amid sector-wide AI-deflation fears reignited by Accenture's guidance cut (which dragged Capgemini down >8% in a single session) and investor scrutiny of the WNS-driven leverage increase, even as reported financial guidance was raised; share price ~€107-109 as of early September 2026 against sell-side price targets clustered €117-160 (consensus meaningfully above spot, but targets have been cut roughly 14% over the prior three months)

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 results (July 30, 2026), upgraded from FY2025 results (February 13, 2026) guidance

items.notes: Raised from the FY2025-results guidance of +6.5% to +8.5% cc; inorganic contribution (WNS, Cloud4C) now estimated at ~5 points (up from ~4.5-5 points originally). Management said H1 performance was 'slightly ahead of expectations.'

Unchanged since FY2025 results despite the restructuring drag on statutory operating profit; management says it is 'confident in delivering' this, supported by Fit-for-Growth initiatives building through H2 2026. FY2025 actual was 13.3%, flat YoY.

Unchanged; explicitly factors in an incremental ~€200m of restructuring cash outflow versus FY2025 related to Fit-for-Growth. FY2025 actual organic FCF was €1,949m (roughly stable YoY), so the FY2026 target implies a modest step-down net of the extra restructuring cash cost.
Country-specific workforce/skills-base initiatives explicitly framed as a response to both weaker demand in certain markets and 'the unprecedented technological disruption driven by AI.'
Per management/press commentary on integration progress; not yet separately quantified in euros in the filings reviewed.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Aiman Ezzat (H1 2026): 'Our first-half performance demonstrates that the strategy we outlined at our Capital Markets Day is delivering results... Agentic AI is now at the center of virtually every client conversation, and Capgemini is recognized as the partner of choice for AI-driven, end-to-end business and operations transformation... With this momentum, we are raising our full year constant currency growth target to around +8.5% to +9.0%. We are confident in delivering our full year margin outlook, supported notably by the implementation of our Fit-for-Growth initiatives, and our organic free cashflow target.' Management explicitly frames the H2 2026 margin build as contingent on Fit-for-Growth benefits materializing, and flags that operating margin 'contracted in continental Europe' in H1 2026 even as North America expanded, i.e., the FY2026 margin guidance requires a Europe-specific inflection in H2 that has not yet shown up in the reported numbers.

bull_case: FY2026 guidance was raised (not cut) at the July 2026 half-year print — constant-currency revenue growth target moved up to +8.5%/+9.0% from +6.5%/+8.5%, with margin and organic-FCF targets maintained, directly contradicting the market's AI-deflation narrative in the near term

France and Continental Europe — half the business and the weakest link for two years — have just inflected to positive organic growth (France +0.4% H1, +1.8% in Q2 2026 alone after five consecutive negative quarters), giving genuine operating leverage upside if the recovery broadens

WNS/Cloud4C position Capgemini as a credible end-to-end 'Intelligent Operations' player combining consulting, technology and now BPO execution at scale, with management citing a 100+ opportunity joint pipeline and 'several large deals secured in recent months' — a differentiated agentic-AI monetization story versus pure IT-services peers
European defense/sovereignty spending is a genuinely new, largely non-discretionary secular tailwind that is idiosyncratic to Capgemini's European base versus US-headquartered competitors

Valuation has compressed sharply (~-30%+ over the trailing year, P/E ~13x, dividend yield support, active buyback) even as guidance has been raised, and sell-side consensus targets (€117-160) sit meaningfully above the ~€107-109 spot price, implying the market may be over-discounting the AI-deflation risk relative to what is showing up in actual bookings/book-to-bill (still >1.0x)
bear_case: Capgemini's own risk disclosures concede the core bear thesis in plain language: Gen/Agentic AI is 'raising external productivity benchmarks more quickly than organizations can adapt,' creating 'pricing to execution mismatches' and reshaping the workforce pyramid — this is a structural, not cyclical, threat to the billable-hours model that underpins Applications & Technology (63% of revenue), and it is why the sector (Accenture's guidance cut, Capgemini's own >8% single-day drop on the read-through) has de-rated hard

The FY2026 growth acceleration is substantially inorganic: roughly 5 of the ~8.5-9.0pts of guided constant-currency growth come from WNS/Cloud4C, and Applications & Technology (the core, highest-margin-potential segment) grew only +5.0% cc in H1 2026 versus Operations & Engineering's +24.7% (largely BPO/WNS) — underlying organic momentum in the core business remains modest

Balance sheet risk has increased sharply and coincides with the point of maximum AI-disruption uncertainty: net debt roughly tripled from €2.1bn (Dec-2024) to €6.5bn (June-2026), gross borrowings exceed €9bn, and goodwill (€14.7bn at June-2026) now exceeds total shareholders' equity (€11.6bn) — leaving limited margin for error if WNS integration or BPO-segment margins disappoint

FY2026 margin guidance (13.6-13.8%) requires a second-half inflection in Continental Europe that has not yet appeared — H1 2026 showed margin CONTRACTION in France (7.7% vs 10.0%) and Rest of Europe (9.6% vs 10.4%), with management attributing the promised improvement to Fit-for-Growth initiatives that are still ramping and cost ~€700m cumulative to execute

Statutory profitability is deteriorating even as the 'operating margin' APM holds up: H1 2026 operating profit -10.1%, net profit -31.3%, normalized EPS -11.9%, organic free cash flow collapsed to just €37m — the APM operating-margin KPI management guides on structurally excludes the restructuring and acquisition-integration costs that are actually depressing GAAP-comparable earnings and cash generation right now
